evidence.quote: They do not intend it to make Owner's payment a condition precedent to Contractor's obligation to pay for Subcontract Work properly performed.

evidence.quote: Contractor shall withhold retention of five percent from each progress payment to Subcontractor.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.1: five percent = 500 bps.

release_condition.value: Final Completion of the Subcontract Work, and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner (subject to conditional final waiver and Article 9 withholdings)

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release all retention withheld from Subcontractor within ten days after both of the following have occurred: Final Completion of the Subcontract Work, and Contractor's receipt of retention from Owner.
evidence.rationale: Section 7.2 sets two triggers; Section 7.3 adds conditional final waiver delivery and Article 9 withholdings; Final Completion depends on Contractor's written confirmation (Section 1.3).

evidence.quote: Contractor shall release all retention withheld from Subcontractor within ten days after both of the following have occurred

evidence.quote: Subcontractor must deliver a Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment (Civil Code Section 8132), covering the amount of the current application, with each application for payment and before Contractor issues any progress payment.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.2 requires a conditional progress waiver with each application.

evidence.quote: After Subcontractor receives each progress payment, Subcontractor must deliver an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment (Civil Code Section 8134) for the amount received.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.3 requires unconditional waivers after each payment.

evidence.quote: Subcontractor must obtain and deliver to Contractor, with each application for payment, conditional and unconditional statutory waivers from each of its sub-subcontractors and material suppliers.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.5 requires lower-tier waivers.

evidence.quote: Every lien waiver and release Subcontractor provides under this Subcontract must be on the applicable statutory form prescribed by California Civil Code Sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138.
evidence.rationale: Section 8.1 mandates California statutory forms.

evidence.quote: Contractor may set off against any amount due to Subcontractor under this Subcontract the amount of any Backcharge.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.2 permits backcharge setoff after written notice and three business days to begin cure, except in emergency.

evidence.quote: Contractor may withhold from any payment an amount reasonably sufficient to correct defective or nonconforming Subcontract Work that Subcontractor has not corrected after notice.
evidence.rationale: Section 9.1 permits withholding for defective work; Section 9.3 adds claims, liens, damage and missing waivers.

evidence.quote: Contractor will not pay for materials or equipment stored on or off the Project site.
evidence.rationale: Section 6.4 states stored materials are not payable.

anomalies.description: Payment and retention periods are written in words only ("seven calendar days", "ten days"), with no numerals; verify the parsed values. Section 7.2 also does not say whether the ten days are calendar or business days.

anomalies.description: Although progress payment timing disclaims a condition precedent, recovery on changes or claims that depend on Owner's action is limited to what Contractor actually recovers from Owner, less Contractor's costs. This shifts Owner non-payment risk to Subcontractor for those amounts.

evidence.quote: To the extent a change or claim depends on Owner's action, Subcontractor's recovery is limited to the amount Contractor actually recovers from Owner on Subcontractor's behalf, less Contractor's reasonable costs of pursuing it.
evidence.rationale: Although progress payment timing disclaims a condition precedent, recovery on changes or claims that depend on Owner's action is limited to what Contractor actually recovers from Owner, less Contractor's costs. This shifts Owner non-payment risk to Subcontractor for those amounts.

anomalies.description: If Owner terminates the Prime Contract, Subcontractor's recovery is limited to a proportionate share of Contractor's recovery from Owner.
